split_note: Split from BANK_GSIB. Represents the non-US G-SIB complex (EU, UK, Switzerland, Japan, China majors) -- internally heterogeneous, but the clearest single documented behavior is jurisdiction-specific improvisation under stress (the Swiss AT1 precedent) rather than either US-style domestic ring-fencing or genuine cross-border coordination. Lower crisis-predictability credibility reflects that heterogeneity directly, not a single coherent strategy.
horizon_driver: Quarterly earnings and Basel/EBA stress tests set the normal cadence; national resolution authorities (FINMA, EU SRB, BoE) can and do act unilaterally and divergently within days once stress is acute -- Credit Suisse's forced UBS sale was executed in roughly a week in March 2023.

constraints.source: Switzerland wrote off CHF16bn (~$17.2bn) of Credit Suisse AT1 bonds ahead of equity in the Mar 2023 UBS merger, overriding the standard absolute-priority rule; the EU (ECB/EBA) and Bank of England issued explicit public statements within days rejecting the Swiss approach for their own jurisdictions (BoE statement, 20 Mar 2023).
constraints.breaks_under: acute national solvency crisis where the home regulator judges creditor-hierarchy deviation necessary over a single weekend -- a Swiss court subsequently ruled the AT1 write-off unlawful (Nov 2025), and US bondholders are still suing Switzerland in 2026, three years later

constraints.source: No EU-UK-Swiss-Japan joint rescue mechanism existed or was invoked in 2023; each jurisdiction acted through its own domestic authority.
constraints.breaks_under: not observed to break; the EU's own Banking Union remains incomplete on cross-border resolution funding as of 2026

stated_vs_revealed.stated: Non-US G-SIBs operate under a harmonised Basel/FSB resolution framework alongside US peers, implying broadly consistent treatment.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: In March 2023 Switzerland unilaterally inverted its own creditor waterfall while the EU and UK immediately and publicly repudiated that approach for their own jurisdictions -- three different non-US authorities took three different positions within the same fortnight.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: The 'coordinated non-US bloc' framing is false; behavior is jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction and reactive, not a bloc strategy.

tripwires.if: a non-US G-SIB faces an acute solvency or deposit-run event
tripwires.then: expect the home regulator to improvise a jurisdiction-specific solution (up to and including creditor-hierarchy deviation, per the Swiss precedent) rather than invoke a coordinated multinational mechanism

tripwires.if: a national regulator forces a bail-in deviating from stated hierarchy
tripwires.then: expect years of cross-border litigation and a lasting repricing of that instrument class globally -- the Credit Suisse AT1 market took until UBS's Jan 2026 return issuance to normalise

what_would_change_my_mind: Direct evidence that post-2023 Basel Committee or EU Banking Union reforms have produced a binding, tested cross-border backstop would raise confidence that this bloc could act more coherently in a future crisis.
